bundle.label: measured
bundle.method: Bytes of each /res/mapstudio/* file as the dev Gateway served it during a page load of the dev map at / (response body decoded, gzip of that body, and the body bytes actually transferred), plus the .modl in ops/modules, the file the Gateway was given (name and SHA-256 recorded). Production webpack build, unsigned. File sizes do not depend on the viewport.
bundle.note: transferredBodyBytes 0 on maplibre-gl-worker.js: Playwright reported no body transfer for the worker request (Chromium fetches a worker script outside the page; why is unverified). Use bytes and gzipBytes for that file.

frameRate.label: measured
frameRate.method: requestAnimationFrame timestamps and long tasks sampled in the page while Playwright drives a 4 s circular drag (at most 60 mouse moves per second) and a 4 s wheel zoom (at most 25 wheel events per second, so about 25 when the page keeps up and fewer when it does not; in for 2 s then out for 2 s) on the map, after a 2 s warm-up; 3 runs on / with the seeded map store items (one view since epic 2 story 11; drawn counts the points and lines MapLibre held). The driver's input events are handled on the page's main thread, so that load shares it with rendering and is the same in every run. Frames are the page's frame cadence during the gesture, not MapLibre's own render count (the map object is not reachable by design).

seeded.stage: map store items from the dev seed (epic 2 story 11): the 30-pad set (30 pads, 30 lines) and the tracer's 3 points and 1 line, plus any items earlier specs saved inside the view; circle and line layers only

limits: Software WebGL (CPU rendered): a laptop GPU is expected to do better, which is unverified here.
Only circle and line layers: no icons, labels, KPI values or alarm styling.
The pads are the dev seed's 30-pad set at the spike stand-in's coordinates, not the template's own set, which this repository cannot read.
frameRate.note: The run-to-run spread on software WebGL is recorded in docs/platform-checks.md, section "Story 7". NFR-1 asks for 60 frames per second in a laptop browser; the renderer this ran on is in env.renderer.

valueBatch.label: measured
valueBatch.method: Playwright websocket frame sizes of the Perspective session socket on /live (an anonymous viewer): the frame that carries the full values.batch sent after map.load (every planned map item and the kind display), and the first changes-only values.batch after a map editor toggled one dev tag. Bytes are the frame's UTF-8 text as received (Perspective wraps the envelope in its own message); gzip of the same text is the best case, not the wire.

changesOnly.rule: the map items whose values changed since the last batch

phone.label: measured
phone.method: Chromium with isMobile and hasTouch at 390x844 (device scale factor 2) on the dev map at / with the seeded items (the line-tool probe on /edit, where Edit mode holds the tool); each probe records ok and a detail, and a failed probe is a finding, not a test failure. Touch moves go through CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent and Input.synthesizePinchGesture; whether they match a real device's touch handling is unverified. Pan and pinch are read from the open popup's tip position (a DOM stand-in for the point's map position), not from the map's centre or zoom, which the suite cannot reach by design.

findings.detail: Zoom in 44x44; Zoom out 44x44; Fit the map to every item 44x44; Return to the selected item 44x44; Legend 94x44
reply text and popup view shown after a touch tap
popup tip moved -93 px horizontally for a 120 px leftward touch drag (needs under -72); the tip is the stand-in for the point's map position
popup tip distance from the pinch centre grew by a factor of 2.36 for a CDP pinch of scale 2 (needs over 1.5)
data-line-points after two vertex taps and a repeat tap on the last, on /edit: '2' (whether Terra Draw finishes this way on touch is the thing probed)
